predecessors.note: The infobox says 'Preceded by: Bushong culture'; the kingdom began as 'a set of chiefdoms with no central authority'. No dossier is implied.

land.text: about 100,000 km2: 'the Kuba sustained their federation of about 100,000 square kilometers' (Early Congolese history); the region 'bordered by the Sankuru, Lulua, and Kasai rivers'

successors.note: The infobox names the International Association of the Congo as successor and ends the kingdom in 1884, but the text says it 'still exists' (current king Kot-a-Mbweeky III 'since 1968') and the Early Congolese history page says that after the Free State was established in 1885 the Kuba 'sustained their federation of about 100,000 square kilometers'. The effective Free State conquest is not dated by any page opened.

capitals.name: Nsheng (Mushenge)
capitals.note: APPROXIMATE: the Early Congolese history page gives 'Capital: Nsheng (modern Mushenge)'; the Mushenge page did not load and no page gives coordinates, so the point is the gazetteer's Mweka (Kasai), a placeholder to be replaced.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Kuba): the page names only the bounding rivers (Sankuru, Lulua, Kasai) and gives no area; the Early Congolese history page gives about 100,000 km2 for the federation after 1885. The gazetteer's Kasai region (281,000 km2, ratio 2.8) is too large, so a 178 km disc (about 100,000 km2) at a placeholder centre is used for the whole life (confidence 1).

region.text: about 100,000 km2: 'the Kuba sustained their federation of about 100,000 square kilometers' (Early Congolese history); the region 'bordered by the Sankuru, Lulua, and Kasai rivers'

ledger.note: c. 1625: Shyaam a-Mbul a Ngoong unites the Kuba chiefdoms. Infobox 'Established: 1625'; 'In approximately 1625, an individual from outside the area known as Shyaam a-Mbul a Ngoong' united the chiefdoms under one leader. The shape is a proxy of about 100,000 km2.

region.text: power extended 'southward along the Kasai River'

ledger.note: 18th century: the Kuba expand south along the Kasai. 'Early in the 18th century, the ruler of Kuba was Kuete M'bogi'; 'This expansion was continued under Koto Nche who was also a king of Kuba during the 18th century.' The page gives no year; 1700 is a bridge (confidence 1). The kingdom 'reached its apex during the mid-19th century'.

region.text: about 100,000 km2: 'the Kuba sustained their federation of about 100,000 square kilometers' (Early Congolese history); the region 'bordered by the Sankuru, Lulua, and Kasai rivers'

ledger.note: 1884: the infobox ends the Kuba Kingdom. 'Europeans first reached the area in 1884'; infobox 'Disestablished: 1884', succeeded by the International Association of the Congo. The text contradicts it (the kingdom still exists); the Early Congolese history page has the federation intact after 1885.

certainty.note: No frontier is given beyond the three bounding rivers.

notes: Cliopatria has no Kuba. The shape is a 178 km disc (about 100,000 km2) at the gazetteer's Mweka, not at Mushenge (no coordinates on any page opened; the Mushenge page failed to load), so the location is approximate. The page's own end (1884) is contradicted by its text and by the Early Congolese history page; the Free State conquest (c. 1900) is not on any page opened. Gazetteer: the region 'Kasai' (alias Kuba) is too large (281,000 km2); 'Mushenge' is not a place. Page budget (2-5): two pages (plus the failed Mushenge page).
